projects.title: Qdrant
projects.question: How do I get a reviewed PR into Qdrant's Rust vector search engine, from a cargo build to the filtered HNSW search path?

steps.title: Frame a Qdrant contribution: dev branch, AI rules, Discord
steps.learn: Aim at lib/segment (indexing and search). Success is a PR that passes CI and gets review. All PRs must target dev; master is release-only. There is no CLA: contributions fall under Apache-2.0. Newcomer labels are sparse (good first issue, help wanted), so expect to find work via bug reports and Discord.
verify: Read docs/CONTRIBUTING.md including the Contributing with AI section
Confirm your fork branch is created from dev, not master
Join the Qdrant Discord and find the channel where contributors ask questions

steps.title: Build Qdrant with cargo and run Rust and Python tests
steps.learn: DEVELOPMENT.md lists Rust, rustfmt, clang, cmake and protoc, then cargo build --release --bin qdrant; CLAUDE.md advises a debug build locally because fat LTO makes --release slow. Rust tests run per crate (cargo test -p segment); Python API tests use uv --project tests run pytest tests/openapi against a server.

decision.choice: Native cargo debug build plus cargo test -p for the crate you touch
decision.why: A debug build and per-crate tests give the fastest edit-compile-test loop, and the repo's own notes say cargo test -p is much faster than the whole workspace.

alternatives.name: docker build . --tag=qdrant/qdrant
alternatives.tradeoff: No local toolchain needed, but every change means a slow image rebuild; good for running, poor for iterating.

alternatives.name: nix-shell
alternatives.tradeoff: Reproducible deps for Rust and Python tests in one command, but requires Nix on your machine.

alternatives.name: --profile perf build
alternatives.tradeoff: Release optimizations without LTO; use it for benchmarks, not for every test run.

steps.delegate: Write a bash script for a Qdrant checkout on branch dev that checks rustc, protoc and uv are installed, runs cargo build --bin qdrant, runs cargo test -p segment, then starts target/debug/qdrant in the background, waits for http://localhost:6333 to respond, runs uv --project tests run pytest tests/openapi/test_filter.py, and stops the server. Fail fast with clear messages.
verify: curl localhost:6333 returns the Qdrant version JSON
cargo test -p segment finishes green on your machine
Record build time, OS and CPU in your notes

steps.title: Trace one filtered query from REST handler to HNSW graph
steps.learn: src/actix/api/query_api.rs calls TableOfContent query_batch in lib/storage/src/content_manager/toc/point_ops.rs, then lib/collection/src/collection/query.rs fans out to shards (shards/local_shard/query.rs), segments are searched, and hnsw/read_view/dispatch.rs in lib/segment picks plain, HNSW or ACORN search.
verify: Load enough points (or lower indexing_threshold) to build HNSW, add a temporary log in dispatch.rs, and see it fire for a filtered query
Write the call chain with one sentence per file
Find where SIMD distance code lives (lib/segment/src/spaces) and name one file

steps.title: Learn filterable HNSW and choose the segment index as target
steps.learn: HNSW is a layered proximity graph searched greedily. Filters break graph connectivity, so Qdrant estimates filter cardinality: if few points match (below full_scan_threshold) it scores them directly, otherwise it searches the graph, adding payload-based links (payload_m) or ACORN for selective filters.

decision.choice: Target lib/segment search and index code
decision.why: Segment code is a self-contained crate with unit tests and criterion benches, so a fix can be tested without a cluster. It is also where vector search ideas (HNSW, filtering, quantization) are most visible.

alternatives.name: REST and gRPC API layer
alternatives.tradeoff: Easier entry, but API changes require openapi specs, schema generator, and endpoint allow lists in sync.

alternatives.name: Consensus and shard transfer (lib/storage, lib/collection)
alternatives.tradeoff: Rich distributed systems work, but bugs need multi-node tests in tests/consensus_tests.

alternatives.name: Qdrant Edge (lib/edge)
alternatives.tradeoff: Newer embeddable shard; changes must update Rust, Python and FFI interfaces together.

verify: Explain why a very selective filter can make pure HNSW search miss results
Find full_scan_threshold handling in dispatch.rs
Read the HNSW paper abstract and Qdrant's filtrable HNSW article

steps.title: Ship a first test or developer-docs PR against dev
steps.learn: With few good first issue labels, a small first PR is often a missing test for an existing behavior, a fix to DEVELOPMENT.md, or a typo caught by the codespell CI job. User docs are on qdrant.tech, not in this repo.

decision.choice: Add a missing test in tests/openapi or a lib/segment unit test for existing behavior
decision.why: Tests need no design discussion, teach you the fixtures, and are cheap to review, so they build trust before a behavior change.

alternatives.name: Developer docs fix
alternatives.tradeoff: Smallest diff, but teaches little about the code.

alternatives.name: Pick a help wanted issue
alternatives.tradeoff: More impact, but these can need design input; ask on the issue first.

verify: Your branch is based on dev and the PR targets dev
The new test passes locally and would fail if the behavior broke
You searched open PRs to confirm nobody already did this

steps.title: Reproduce a segment or filter bug as a failing test
steps.learn: Filter open issues by bug plus an area label (area/segment, area/payload-index, area/storage) with recent activity and no assignee; skip ones marked needs-decision or needs-info. Rebuild the repro as a script against a local server, then shrink it to a Rust unit test or an openapi pytest.

decision.choice: Minimal Python repro first, then a Rust unit test in lib/segment
decision.why: Most reports arrive as client calls, so a pytest against the REST API confirms the bug fast; moving it to a Rust test pins it to the segment layer and runs without a server.

alternatives.name: Keep only the tests/openapi pytest
alternatives.tradeoff: Covers the full stack, but needs a running server and hides which layer is at fault.

alternatives.name: Consensus test in tests/consensus_tests
alternatives.tradeoff: Needed for multi-node bugs, but spawns a cluster and is slow to iterate.

verify: The repro fails on the current dev branch
The test fails for the reason in the issue, not a setup error
You posted the minimal repro on the issue before fixing

steps.title: Fix the bug in Rust with the failing test committed first
steps.learn: Follow .github/review-rules.md: explicit Type::from over .into(), exhaustive matches over catch-all arms, bytemuck or zerocopy instead of the transmute helpers. Per CONTRIBUTING, list AI-made commits as [AI] and manual ones as [manual], share your initial prompt, and write the PR motivation yourself.
steps.delegate: In qdrant/qdrant (branch dev), the test <name> in lib/segment fails because <symptom>. Run cargo test -p segment <name> to confirm. Find the root cause and make the smallest fix. Follow .github/review-rules.md (explicit From, exhaustive matches, no transmute helpers). Run cargo +nightly fmt --all and cargo clippy -p segment --all-targets -- -D warnings. Explain the root cause in 3 sentences and list changed files.
verify: You can explain every changed line without notes
The new test fails on dev and passes with your fix
Commits are labeled [AI] or [manual] in your PR notes

steps.title: Pass rustfmt, clippy, ast-grep and nextest like CI does
steps.learn: rust-lint.yml runs cargo +nightly fmt --all -- --check, clippy with -D warnings (workspace, all targets, all features) and ast-grep (sg scan with tools/ast-grep/sgconfig.yml). rust.yml runs cargo nextest with the ci profile in .config/nextest.toml; integration tests use tests/integration-tests.sh and pytest.
verify: cargo +nightly fmt --all -- --check is clean
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings is clean
sg scan --config tools/ast-grep/sgconfig.yml reports nothing on your diff

steps.title: Benchmark the change with criterion and Tango benches
steps.learn: Benches are not in CI, so run the ones your change touches: cargo bench --bench <name> inside lib/segment (for example hnsw_search_graph or conditional_search). Criterion prints change with a p-value; Tango benches compare two binaries side by side. Use --profile-time for flamegraphs.

decision.choice: Criterion bench in lib/segment/benches, with a Tango compare run if one exists for the code
decision.why: These are the harnesses DEVELOPMENT.md documents, so maintainers can rerun your numbers; Tango's paired runs reduce noise from machine drift.

alternatives.name: qdrant/vector-db-benchmark
alternatives.tradeoff: End to end numbers on real datasets, but slower and noisier for a small code change.

alternatives.name: Ad hoc timing in a test
alternatives.tradeoff: Quick to write, but no warmup or statistics and maintainers cannot reproduce it.

verify: You report criterion's interval and p-value for before and after
Both runs used the same machine, CPU governor and build profile
You state the CPU model and whether AVX or NEON paths were used

steps.title: Open the PR against dev and handle review
steps.learn: Fill the PR template checklist (dev base, fmt, clippy, tests) and explain why the change is needed in your own words. An automated CodeRabbit check runs alongside rust-tests, lint and integration jobs. Rebase on dev when asked and keep commits small. If review stalls, ask politely on Discord.

decision.choice: One focused PR, rebased on dev, with separate commits per logical change
decision.why: CONTRIBUTING asks for incremental changes as separate commits so reviewers can follow intent, and a small diff is easier to review with limited maintainer time.

alternatives.name: Squash into a single commit
alternatives.tradeoff: Cleaner history, but hides which parts were AI-assisted or manual, which CONTRIBUTING asks you to show.

alternatives.name: Draft PR for early feedback
alternatives.tradeoff: Useful for design questions, but maintainers may not look until it is marked ready.

verify: The PR base branch is dev
All CI checks are green or failures are shown to be unrelated
Each review comment has a code change or a reply

steps.title: Write up the Qdrant fix and pick the next rung
steps.learn: Record the bug, which layer was wrong, what the review changed, and benchmark numbers with the machine. Next rungs: a filtering or quantization improvement with bench evidence, an API feature that touches openapi and gRPC, or a consensus test.
verify: The write-up names the root cause file and the fix
Every number lists the bench command, machine and spread
You name one concrete next issue or area and why

projects.problem: Qdrant is a Rust vector database; contributing teaches HNSW, filtered search planning, segments and a Raft-backed storage layer.
projects.proveIt: A PR against dev that passes fmt, clippy and tests in CI and gets maintainer review, plus a write-up with benchmark numbers
projects.hardware: Linux or macOS machine with a Rust toolchain and protoc; a GPU is only needed for the optional GPU HNSW build
projects.aiPolicy: AI tools are allowed. External contributors must write the PR motivation themselves; disclose AI-generated commits ([AI] vs [manual]) and the initial prompt, and be able to explain the changes.

projects.title: FAISS
projects.question: Can you land a reviewed, tested change in FAISS's HNSW code, the C++ library behind much of today's vector search?

steps.title: Frame a FAISS contribution aimed at the HNSW index
steps.learn: FAISS is developed mainly inside Meta and synced to GitHub. Outside PRs need the Meta CLA, are imported by a bot into Meta's internal test suite, then closed with a Merged label rather than merged on GitHub. CONTRIBUTING asks you to contact maintainers first for major work. No AI policy file was found.
verify: You have read CONTRIBUTING.md and can state its six PR steps and its style rules (4 spaces, 80 columns, C++20)
You have signed the Meta CLA at code.facebook.com/cla with the GitHub account you will use
You have read CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, know CONTRIBUTING.md sends bugs to Issues, and found GitHub Discussions for questions
You wrote down the success measure: a PR that passes CI and gets a maintainer response, with a merge as the stretch goal

steps.title: Build FAISS with CMake and run the C++ and Python tests
steps.learn: INSTALL.md: cmake -B build ., make -C build -j faiss, make -C build -j swigfaiss, then (cd build/faiss/python && python setup.py build). Test with make -C build test and pytest tests/test_*.py with PYTHONPATH set to build/faiss/python/build/lib*. Needs SWIG and numpy.

decision.choice: CPU-only CMake build with -DFAISS_ENABLE_GPU=OFF, -DBUILD_TESTING=ON and Release mode
decision.why: The HNSW code is CPU-only, a GPU build adds the CUDA toolkit and long compile times for nothing you will touch, and a source build is the only way to run your own changes against the C++ and Python tests the way CI does.

alternatives.name: conda install faiss-cpu (or the nightly)
alternatives.tradeoff: Fastest way to use FAISS from Python, but you cannot test a change to the C++ code, so it only suits pure docs or contrib work.

alternatives.name: Full GPU build with CUDA
alternatives.tradeoff: Needed only if you target faiss/gpu; requires nvcc, an NVIDIA GPU and much longer builds, and CI runs these jobs on T4 runners.

verify: make -C build test finishes and you record how many C++ tests passed
pytest tests/test_hnsw.py passes against your freshly built bindings, not a conda-installed faiss
python -c 'import faiss; print(faiss.__file__)' points into your build directory

steps.title: Trace one HNSW search from Python down to the graph walk
steps.learn: index.search in Python goes through replacement_search in faiss/python/class_wrappers.py into SWIG (faiss/python/swigfaiss.swig), then IndexHNSW::search in faiss/IndexHNSW.cpp, which calls hnsw_search and HNSW::search in faiss/impl/HNSW.cpp with a DistanceComputer from the storage index.
verify: You can name the file and function at each hop from Python index.search to HNSW::search
You found where efSearch is read (HNSW.h and SearchParametersHNSW) and where efConstruction is used
You built IndexHNSWFlat via index_factory('HNSW32,Flat') and stepped into HNSW::search in a debugger or with prints

steps.title: Learn the HNSW graph and pick the FAISS subsystem to target
steps.learn: HNSW builds a layered proximity graph; search descends greedily through upper layers, then runs a beam search of width efSearch on layer 0. In FAISS the graph sits on a storage index (Flat, PQ, SQ), so distance computation and graph walk are separate. The Faiss library paper explains the index families.

decision.choice: Target CPU HNSW: faiss/IndexHNSW.* and faiss/impl/HNSW.* with their tests
decision.why: It is a self-contained, CPU-only path with Python and C++ tests (tests/test_hnsw.py, tests/test_hnsw.cpp) and benchmark scripts, so you can show correctness and speed on one machine without a GPU.

alternatives.name: IVF and quantizers (IndexIVF*, PQ, RaBitQ)
alternatives.tradeoff: The largest and most active area with many index variants; more to learn, and changes often touch SIMD kernels and serialization formats.

alternatives.name: GPU indices (faiss/gpu)
alternatives.tradeoff: High impact but needs an NVIDIA GPU and CUDA builds, and parts now route to NVIDIA cuVS.

alternatives.name: Python contrib (contrib/)
alternatives.tradeoff: Pure Python and easy to test, but less exposure to the C++ core.

verify: You can explain in two sentences why raising efSearch increases recall and latency
You measured recall@10 of HNSW32,Flat against IndexFlatL2 on a small random set for two efSearch values

steps.title: Ship a small docs or test PR to learn the FAISS import flow
steps.learn: Because every PR goes through the CLA check and an internal import, a tiny first PR teaches the process cheaply. FAISS has a documentation label and an ez label (very few open). Docs live in header comments (rendered at faiss.ai) and the wiki; the wiki is not edited through PRs.

decision.choice: Add or tighten a test for HNSW behavior that is documented but untested
decision.why: Tests in tests/test_hnsw.py are easy to review, cannot break users, and force you to run the Python suite exactly as CI does.

alternatives.name: Fix a header doc comment
alternatives.tradeoff: Smallest possible diff and rendered on faiss.ai, but teaches little about the build or tests.

alternatives.name: Fix an issue labeled documentation
alternatives.tradeoff: Answers a real user need, but some are questions best handled in the wiki, which is not changed by PR.

verify: Your test fails if you deliberately break the behavior it checks, and passes otherwise
The PR shows the CLA Signed label and you note how long until a maintainer responded

steps.title: Reproduce an HNSW issue as a failing pytest or gtest case
steps.learn: Look at issues labeled bug or GPU and recent unlabeled HNSW reports; prefer ones with recent activity, no linked PR and a clear reproduction. The issue template asks for OS, FAISS commit, install method, CPU or GPU and C++ or Python, so collect the same facts for your repro.

decision.choice: Write the repro as a Python unittest in tests/ that uses small random data with a fixed seed
decision.why: FAISS tests mostly compare an approximate index to IndexFlat on seeded random data; matching that style makes the repro become the regression test with no extra work.

alternatives.name: C++ gtest in tests/test_hnsw.cpp
alternatives.tradeoff: Best when the bug is below the SWIG layer or in threading; slower edit and build loop.

alternatives.name: Standalone script in the issue
alternatives.tradeoff: Quick to share, but must still be turned into a test before a PR.

verify: The repro fails on current main built from source and you recorded the commit hash
It runs in under a few seconds and does not download data
You commented on the issue with the minimal repro before starting the fix

steps.title: Fix the HNSW bug with a test that fails first
steps.learn: Keep the fix inside the subsystem you traced. Changes to index structure fields can affect serialization in faiss/impl/index_read.cpp and index_write.cpp, and CI checks index I/O backward compatibility, so avoid format changes in a first fix. You must understand and defend every line.
steps.delegate: In facebookresearch/faiss (C++20, 4-space indent, 80 columns, clang-format per .clang-format; Python black width 80 and flake8 per faiss/.flake8), first add a failing test to tests/test_hnsw.py (unittest, seeded random data, compare against IndexFlatL2) for this bug: <paste repro>. Then fix it minimally in faiss/impl/HNSW.cpp or faiss/IndexHNSW.cpp without changing the serialized format. Explain each changed line.
verify: The new test fails before the fix and passes after, on your own build
git diff touches only the files you expected and has no unrelated formatting changes
You can explain every changed line to a reviewer without the agent

steps.title: Run clang-format, flake8 and the CI test subset locally
steps.learn: build-pull-request.yml runs a Format job with clang-format 21 over all .cpp/.h/.cu/.cuh files and fails on any diff, then cmake builds that run make -C build test and pytest tests/test_*.py. AVX2, AVX512, ARM SVE, Windows, Metal and GPU jobs run only on matching runners, so you cannot reproduce all of them locally.
verify: clang-format-21 -i on your changed C++ files leaves git diff unchanged
flake8 with faiss/.flake8 reports nothing for your changed Python files
make -C build test and pytest tests/test_hnsw.py both pass on your build
If you have AVX2, a -DFAISS_OPT_LEVEL=avx2 build also passes the HNSW tests

steps.title: Measure HNSW recall and latency before and after on SIFT1M
steps.learn: benchs/bench_hnsw.py runs HNSW on SIFT1M via faiss.contrib.datasets, which reads data/sift1M/ (not the root sift1M/ in INSTALL.md); perf_tests/bench_hnsw.py is an argparse benchmark. Pin OMP_NUM_THREADS, repeat runs and report recall with every timing.

decision.choice: Use benchs/bench_hnsw.py on SIFT1M with fixed threads and 5 repeats per build
decision.why: It is the repo's own HNSW benchmark on a standard dataset with ground truth, so reviewers can rerun it and recall changes are visible next to speed.

alternatives.name: perf_tests/bench_hnsw.py
alternatives.tradeoff: More configurable via flags; better for sweeping parameters, less familiar output for reviewers.

alternatives.name: Random data micro-benchmark
alternatives.tradeoff: No download and quick, but random vectors behave differently from real embeddings and can hide recall effects.

verify: You report median and spread of search time over at least 5 runs for both builds
Recall at the same efSearch is unchanged, or the change is explained
The write-up records CPU model, core count, OMP_NUM_THREADS, BLAS and the exact command

steps.title: Open the FAISS PR and follow it through internal import
steps.learn: There is no PR template, so write the summary yourself: link the issue, show the failing test and the benchmark table. After a maintainer imports it, meta-codesync posts comments and the PR is closed with a Merged label once it lands internally. Fixes may be requested in the PR.

decision.choice: One focused PR from a branch off main, rebased rather than merged when main moves
decision.why: Internal import works best on small, linear diffs, and a short PR is easier for a busy team to review.

alternatives.name: Open a Discussion or issue first
alternatives.tradeoff: Required in spirit for anything large per CONTRIBUTING; costs a round trip but avoids wasted work.

alternatives.name: Bundle related fixes
alternatives.tradeoff: Fewer PRs, but harder to review and import, and one blocker stalls all of them.

verify: The PR description links the issue, states the test added and includes before and after numbers
All GitHub CI jobs triggered for your change are green and CLA Signed is present
You answered every review comment within a few days, and pinged politely once if it sat two weeks

steps.title: Write up the FAISS contribution and choose the next rung
steps.learn: Record what you learned about the HNSW code and the import process, with numbers. Good next rungs: an HNSW search parameter or stats improvement, an IVF or quantizer bug, or a GPU index issue if you have the hardware.
verify: The write-up states the question, the change, and benchmark numbers with machine and command
It explains one surprise you hit in the codebase or the review
It names a concrete next issue or subsystem and why

projects.problem: FAISS is Meta's C++/Python library for vector similarity search and clustering; contributing teaches ANN index internals, SWIG bindings and SIMD code
projects.proveIt: A PR with a test that passes FAISS CI and gets imported or reviewed by a maintainer, plus a write-up with recall and latency numbers
projects.hardware: Linux, macOS or Windows with a C++20 compiler, OpenMP and BLAS for CPU work; a CUDA or ROCm GPU only for faiss/gpu

projects.title: hnswlib
projects.question: Can you land a reviewed fix in hnswlib, the small header-only HNSW library many vector databases have learned from?

steps.title: Frame an hnswlib contribution and its develop-branch rules
steps.learn: PRs must target develop, not the default master, and CONTRIBUTING.md exists only on develop. There is no CLA, DCO, code of conduct or AI policy file. Maintainers talk only in issues and PRs. Expect slow review: many open PRs, and maintainers often rebase outside PRs themselves.
verify: You read CONTRIBUTING.md on develop and can list its pre-submit checklist
You know the license is Apache-2.0 and that no CLA or sign-off is required
You wrote down the success measure: a CI-green PR on develop with maintainer review, a merge as stretch goal

steps.title: Build hnswlib's Python and C++ targets and run both tests
steps.learn: make install runs pip install . for the pybind11 extension; make test runs tests/python/bindings_test*.py and make examples runs examples/python. C++ tests build with cmake .. -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo in build/ then ctest; test_updates needs data from tests/cpp/update_gen_data.py.

decision.choice: Both: pip install . for Python tests and a RelWithDebInfo CMake build for ctest
decision.why: The core is header-only and shared by both, so a C++ change must pass ctest and the Python bindings tests; CI runs both on three OSes.

alternatives.name: pip install hnswlib from PyPI
alternatives.tradeoff: Instant, but tests the released code, not your branch.

alternatives.name: HNSWLIB_NATIVE=1 pip install .
alternatives.tradeoff: Adds -march=native for a machine-local build; the default build omits it and picks SIMD kernels at runtime (HNSWLIB_SIMD can force a lower level).

verify: make test and make examples pass on your develop checkout
ctest --output-on-failure passes in build/ and you ran ./test_updates and ./test_updates update
You built once with -DHNSWLIB_ENABLE_EXCEPTIONS=OFF and ctest still passes

steps.title: Trace knn_query from Python into searchBaseLayerST
steps.learn: knn_query in python_bindings/bindings.cpp calls searchKnn (hnswlib.h), which wraps HierarchicalNSW::searchKnnNoExceptions in hnswalg.h: greedy descent of upper layers, then searchBaseLayerST. Inserts: addPoint, getRandomLevel, searchBaseLayer, getNeighborsByHeuristic2, mutuallyConnectNewElement.
verify: You can name the function at each hop from knn_query to searchBaseLayerST
You found where ef and ef_construction are stored and where the visited list pool is used
You can say which locks addPoint takes (link_list_locks_, label_op_locks_, global)

steps.title: Learn HNSW parameters and pick the hnswlib area to target
steps.learn: ALGO_PARAMS.md explains M, ef_construction and ef and gives a check: recall for M neighbors at ef equal to ef_construction should be at least 0.9. The HNSW paper gives the neighbor selection heuristic implemented by getNeighborsByHeuristic2. CONTRIBUTING documents the threading rules.

decision.choice: Target correctness in the core: deletes, replace_deleted, filtering or serialization in hnswalg.h
decision.why: These paths have dedicated tests (bindings_test_replace, bindings_test_filter, loadindex_corruption) and recent fixes, so a well-tested fix is valued and checkable on a laptop-class machine.

alternatives.name: SIMD distance kernels (space_l2.h, space_ip.h)
alternatives.tradeoff: Clear speed wins possible, but must stay behind USE_SSE/USE_AVX/USE_AVX512 guards and pass on MSVC, GCC and Clang.

alternatives.name: Python bindings (bindings.cpp)
alternatives.tradeoff: Visible API improvements, but changes the user-facing surface and needs careful review.

verify: You ran the ALGO_PARAMS.md check on random data and recorded the recall
You can explain why mixing insert and search concurrently is unsafe here

steps.title: Ship a small test or example PR to hnswlib
steps.learn: New tests go in tests/python/bindings_test_*.py (auto discovered) or tests/cpp/*_test.cpp registered in TEST_NAMES in CMakeLists.txt; Python examples in examples/python/example*.py run in CI. Labels are rarely applied, so labels alone will not find work.

decision.choice: Add a Python test that covers an untested documented behavior of the bindings
decision.why: It needs no C++ API change, runs on every CI job, and shows maintainers you follow their layout before you send a core change.

alternatives.name: Add or fix an example
alternatives.tradeoff: Useful for users and checked by make examples, but less likely to catch real bugs.

alternatives.name: Fix a README or TESTING_RECALL.md error
alternatives.tradeoff: Smallest diff; low risk but teaches little about the code.

verify: The new test fails if you break the behavior on purpose
make test passes and the PR targets develop with Allow edits from maintainers checked

steps.title: Reproduce an hnswlib bug as a minimal failing test
steps.learn: Only a couple of old issues carry help wanted, so read recent unlabeled issues for crashes, wrong results or recall regressions, and check open PRs to avoid duplicates. CONTRIBUTING asks reports to include version, OS, compiler or Python, and for recall issues M, ef_construction, ef, dim and data size.

decision.choice: Write the repro as a unittest in tests/python with seeded random data and BFIndex as ground truth
decision.why: BFIndex gives exact neighbors in the same API, so the repro is self-contained and becomes the regression test.

alternatives.name: C++ test under ASan/UBSan
alternatives.tradeoff: Best for memory or alignment bugs (-DENABLE_ASAN=ON -DENABLE_UBSAN=ON); Linux only and slower to iterate.

alternatives.name: ThreadSanitizer build
alternatives.tradeoff: Needed for races (-DENABLE_TSAN=ON); not in the default CI matrix, so explain it in the PR.

verify: The repro fails on current develop and you recorded the commit hash
No open PR already fixes the same issue
You posted the minimal repro on the issue

steps.title: Fix the hnswlib bug with a failing test first
steps.learn: hnswlib/ is header-only C++11 with no external dependencies and must compile cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror. Throwing methods wrap *NoExceptions methods that return Status, so fix the logic once there and test both forms. Understand and defend every line.
steps.delegate: In nmslib/hnswlib on a branch from upstream/develop, add a failing test first (tests/python/bindings_test_<name>.py using unittest, or tests/cpp/<name>_test.cpp registered in TEST_NAMES) for: <paste repro>. Then fix hnswlib/hnswalg.h minimally, keeping C++11, no new dependencies, warning-free under -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror, with the logic in the *NoExceptions or internal code the throwing wrappers call. Use existing locks for new state.
verify: The new test fails before and passes after the fix
The diff changes no unrelated lines and adds no dependency
You can explain the fix and its thread-safety without the agent

steps.title: Run hnswlib's exception, sanitizer and compiler matrix
steps.learn: CI runs Python 3.9 to 3.13 on Ubuntu, Windows and macOS, and C++ across OS, compilers (gcc, clang, msvc), ASan plus UBSan, exceptions on and off, plus a C++17 job. test_all_build_types.sh runs the clang/gcc times sanitizer times build type matrix locally and needs Ninja.
verify: ctest passes with HNSWLIB_ENABLE_EXCEPTIONS ON and OFF
A build with -DENABLE_ASAN=ON -DENABLE_UBSAN=ON passes ctest on Linux
./test_all_build_types.sh completes, or you note which compilers you lacked
make test and make examples pass

steps.title: Measure hnswlib speed and recall before and after
steps.learn: tests/python/speedtest.py times queries on seeded random data with -d dim, -n name and -t threads; git_tester.py replays it across commits with pydriller. bindings_test_recall.py compares against BFIndex. README describes a 200M SIFT test via tests/cpp/download_bigann.py, too large for most laptops.

decision.choice: speedtest.py for timing plus a recall check against BFIndex, on fixed threads, 5 runs each
decision.why: These are the repo's own tools, run on any machine without downloads, and pairing recall with time stops a speedup from hiding a quality loss.

alternatives.name: git_tester.py across commits
alternatives.tradeoff: Shows a trend over history, but needs pydriller and rebuilds per commit, so it is slow.

alternatives.name: SIFT 200M C++ test
alternatives.tradeoff: Realistic scale, but needs a very large download, lots of RAM and hours of build time.

steps.title: Open the hnswlib PR against develop and handle review
steps.learn: Use gh pr create --base develop, keep Allow edits from maintainers checked so they can push fixes or rebase, and rebase on upstream/develop before pushing. There is no PR template. All CI checks must pass before merge; maintainers sometimes reopen outside work as their own rebased PR.

decision.choice: A single small PR with the test, the fix and a short numbers table
decision.why: Review bandwidth is limited and many PRs are open, so a small, CI-green PR with clear evidence is the one most likely to be picked up.

alternatives.name: Open an issue first
alternatives.tradeoff: Useful for API or behavior changes, but responses can be slow.

alternatives.name: Larger feature PR
alternatives.tradeoff: More impact, but large outside PRs have often waited a long time or been rebased by maintainers.

steps.learn: Record what you learned about the graph code, the threading rules and the review process, with numbers. Next rungs: a SIMD kernel improvement, a binding feature, or porting the lessons to FAISS's HNSW.

projects.problem: hnswlib is a header-only C++ HNSW library with Python bindings; contributing teaches graph ANN search, concurrency and SIMD in a small codebase
projects.proveIt: A PR against develop that passes the full CI matrix and gets maintainer review, plus a write-up with recall and speed numbers
projects.hardware: Linux, macOS or Windows with a C++11 compiler and Python 3.9 or newer (the CI matrix); sanitizers on Linux; no GPU

projects.title: Tantivy
projects.question: How do you get a tested fix into Tantivy's query engine, from first build to a PR that passes CI and gets maintainer review?

steps.title: Set the target and the house rules for a Tantivy PR
steps.learn: Tantivy is a library, not a server; it is MIT licensed and run by the Quickwit team. There is no CONTRIBUTING file, code of conduct or PR template: the README asks you to reference an issue or write a full commit message. No CLA or DCO check runs on PRs, and no written AI policy exists. Chat happens on Discord.

decision.choice: Aim at the query module (src/query); success is a PR with green CI and maintainer review
decision.why: Queries are self-contained (Query, Weight, Scorer per file), have unit tests next to the code and dedicated benches, so a newcomer can reproduce, fix and measure without touching indexing or storage formats. A merge is the goal but depends on a small maintainer team.

alternatives.name: Aggregations (src/aggregation)
alternatives.tradeoff: Large, user-visible feature surface with JSON request semantics shared with Quickwit; good if you use aggregations, but changes need compatibility care.

alternatives.name: Indexer and merges (src/indexer)
alternatives.tradeoff: Pick it to learn segment lifecycle and concurrency; failpoint and long-running tests make bugs subtle and reviews slower.

verify: Read the README Contributing code section and note what it asks of a PR
Confirm the LICENSE file is MIT and that no CLA bot appears in the checks of a recent merged PR
Join the Discord and find where contributors ask questions
Find at least two recently merged PRs by outside contributors

steps.title: Build Tantivy and run its tests with cargo and nextest
steps.learn: Tantivy compiles on stable Rust (MSRV 1.88). README says clone and run cargo test; make test runs cargo test --tests --lib to skip examples. CI uses cargo nextest with three feature sets: all, quickwit, and none (no default features, --lib only). Failpoint tests live in a separate test binary.

decision.choice: Use cargo nextest with the CI 'all' feature set as your default local test command
decision.why: It matches what the test-all CI job runs (mmap, stopwords, lz4 and zstd compression, failpoints, stemmer, jitexpr with --no-default-features --workspace), so a green local run predicts a green PR and also builds the failpoints binary.

alternatives.name: Plain cargo test
alternatives.tradeoff: Zero setup and the README default; uses default features only, so it skips failpoints and jitexpr code paths that CI exercises.

alternatives.name: make test
alternatives.tradeoff: Fastest loop (lib and tests only, no examples); misses doctests and example compilation, so run the fuller set before pushing.

verify: cargo nextest run with the all feature set finishes with zero failures on main
cargo test --doc with the same features passes
Record clean build time and test time on your machine for later comparison

steps.title: Trace one search through Searcher, Weight, Scorer and Collector
steps.learn: Searcher::search (src/core/searcher.rs) builds a Weight via query.weight, then calls collect_segment per SegmentReader. In src/collector/mod.rs that drives weight.for_each, feeding (doc, score) to collect. TermWeight (src/query/term_query) reads SegmentPostings (src/postings) via the term dictionary (src/termdict).
verify: Run examples/basic_search.rs and set breakpoints in Searcher::search and TermWeight::scorer
Write the call chain as file:function pairs from Searcher::search to Collector::collect
After a commit, list the index directory and match each segment file to a SegmentComponent

steps.title: Learn bitpacked postings, BM25 and block WAND in Tantivy
steps.learn: Postings are blocks of 128 doc ids, delta encoded and bitpacked (SIMD, SSE3), with a variable int tail; an FST maps terms to TermInfo. Scoring is BM25 (src/query/bm25.rs), not configurable. Top-k term and boolean queries skip blocks via block WAND (boolean_query/block_wand_*.rs). Segments are immutable and merged.

decision.choice: Focus on scorers in src/query (term, boolean, phrase) as your subsystem
decision.why: Scorer bugs show up as wrong hits or scores you can assert in a tiny in-RAM index, the DocSet contract (src/docset.rs) is small enough to learn, and benches like and_or_queries and intersection_bench already exist for later performance work.

alternatives.name: Postings and bitpacking crates
alternatives.tradeoff: Deepest performance payoff (src/postings, bitpacking crate); changes touch on-disk format and SIMD paths, so review bar and risk are high.

alternatives.name: Tokenizers (src/tokenizer)
alternatives.tradeoff: Easy to test and language-focused; less about search internals, and many tokenizers live in external crates.

alternatives.name: Query parser (query-grammar crate)
alternatives.tradeoff: Good for parser-combinator experience and has a query-grammar label; behavior changes affect every user's query syntax.

verify: Explain in two sentences why delta encoding makes doc id blocks bitpack well
Point to the code that decides when block WAND is used for a top-k term query
State which BM25 inputs come from fieldnorms and which from TermInfo

links.label: Lemire and Boytsov: vectorized integer decoding

steps.title: Land a rustdoc or example PR on a query type first
steps.learn: Public items are documented on docs.rs and CI runs doctests, so a missing or wrong example is a real, testable fix. The repo has documentation and good first issue labels. examples/ holds runnable programs such as fuzzy_search.rs and phrase_prefix_search.rs that cargo test compiles (not runs) when features are on.

decision.choice: Add or fix a runnable rustdoc example on one query type, checked by doctests
decision.why: It is small, reviewable in minutes, exercises the full fmt, clippy and doctest pipeline, and teaches the public API you will later change. Maintainers can merge it without design discussion.

alternatives.name: New program in examples/
alternatives.tradeoff: More visible and fun; bigger diff and maintainers may question whether the example earns its place.

alternatives.name: Unit test for an untested edge case
alternatives.tradeoff: Pick it if you spot a gap while tracing; needs more context to show the case matters.

steps.delegate: In quickwit-oss/tantivy (Rust 2021, MSRV 1.88), add a runnable rustdoc example to the doc comment of <QueryType> in src/query/<file>.rs. Build an in-RAM index with Index::create_in_ram, add 3 docs, run the query with TopDocs, and assert the hits. Match the style of nearby doc examples. It must pass cargo test --doc --features mmap,stopwords,lz4-compression,zstd-compression,failpoints,stemmer,jitexpr --no-default-features. No public API changes.
verify: The doctest fails if you change the expected hit, proving it really runs
cargo doc renders the example under the right type
cargo +nightly fmt --all -- --check is clean

steps.title: Reproduce a query bug as a failing in-RAM Rust test
steps.learn: Pick an open issue labeled bug or good first issue with recent activity and no assignee, and comment before starting. The bug template asks for the version or sha and minimal reproducing code. Most bugs reproduce in a #[test] with a tiny schema, Index::create_in_ram and a few documents.

decision.choice: Write the repro as a unit test in the affected module's #[cfg(test)] block
decision.why: It runs in milliseconds under nextest, becomes the regression test in your PR, and sits next to the code reviewers will read. In-RAM indexes remove filesystem and mmap noise from the repro.

alternatives.name: Standalone binary on a git dependency
alternatives.tradeoff: Best for reporting from a user's point of view; not mergeable, so you rewrite it as a test later.

alternatives.name: Ignored functional tests (src/functional_test.rs)
alternatives.tradeoff: Randomized long runs catch rare indexing bugs; slow, and CI only runs them on main via long_running.yml.

verify: The new test fails on main for the reason the issue describes, not a setup error
The failure also appears with --no-default-features unless the bug is feature specific
You posted the minimal repro on the issue and got or waited for a maintainer reply

steps.title: Fix the scorer bug at the layer that owns the invariant
steps.learn: Scorers implement DocSet (src/docset.rs): doc ids come out sorted and seek/advance must respect that contract; src/query/seek_danger_tests.rs exists because seeking is easy to get wrong. Fix where the invariant breaks, keep the diff small, and be able to explain every line yourself.

decision.choice: A minimal fix inside the scorer or weight that breaks the contract
decision.why: Small fixes in the owning type are easy to review and keep other queries correct; reviewers on a small team favor diffs they can verify quickly over refactors.

alternatives.name: Workaround in the collector or caller
alternatives.tradeoff: Faster to write; hides the bug for other callers and is likely to be rejected in review.

alternatives.name: Refactor the scorer family
alternatives.tradeoff: Worth it only after maintainers agree on the issue; a much larger diff and longer review.

steps.delegate: Repo quickwit-oss/tantivy, Rust 2021, MSRV 1.88. First add a failing #[test] in <module> reproducing <issue> with an in-RAM index; confirm it fails. Then make the minimal fix, respecting the DocSet contract in src/docset.rs. Format with cargo +nightly fmt --all, keep cargo clippy --tests clean, add no dependencies, change no public API. Run cargo nextest run --workspace. Explain each changed line and why it fixes the root cause.
verify: You can explain every changed line without the agent's notes
The new test fails before the fix and passes after it
The diff touches no files unrelated to the bug

steps.title: Pass fmt, clippy and all three CI feature sets locally
steps.learn: The check job runs cargo +nightly fmt --all -- --check, cargo build --all-features, cargo +nightly bench --no-run --profile=dev --all-features, and clippy with --tests on stable. Test jobs run nextest for the all, quickwit and none feature sets plus doctests. Coverage and Scorecards run only on main, not on PRs.

decision.choice: Run nightly fmt, clippy and all three nextest feature sets before every push
decision.why: The none set (--no-default-features --lib) catches code that silently depends on mmap or compression features, and bench compilation catches API changes that break benches; both are common surprises on a first PR.

alternatives.name: Rely on CI
alternatives.tradeoff: Saves local time; each red run is public and costs a review round trip.

alternatives.name: Default features only
alternatives.tradeoff: Fast loop while iterating; misses feature-gated breakage that the quickwit and none jobs catch.

verify: cargo +nightly fmt --all -- --check prints nothing
cargo clippy --tests shows no new warnings in files you touched
nextest passes for all, quickwit and none feature sets

steps.title: Measure a query change with the binggan and criterion benches
steps.learn: benches/ holds harness=false benches using binggan (and_or_queries, intersection_bench, range_queries) and criterion (index-bench). Run one with cargo bench --bench and_or_queries on main and on your branch. The bench profile keeps debug symbols, which helps flame graphs. search-benchmark-game compares against Lucene.

decision.choice: Use the existing bench closest to your change; extend it only if no case covers it
decision.why: Maintainers already trust these benches, so before and after numbers from them are easy to judge. Adding a case to an existing file is a smaller diff than a new [[bench]] entry in Cargo.toml.

alternatives.name: search-benchmark-game end to end
alternatives.tradeoff: Realistic corpus and Lucene comparison; heavy setup and noisy for small changes.

alternatives.name: New bench file
alternatives.tradeoff: Needed for a new code path; reviewers must agree it has lasting value.

verify: Report main vs branch for each case with spread over at least 3 runs
Record CPU model, OS, rustc version and that the machine was otherwise idle
A flame graph or profile shows where time moved, consistent with your claim

steps.title: Open a small Tantivy PR and work through review
steps.learn: There is no PR template, so the description carries the why, the issue link, the failing test and any numbers. Keep one logical change per PR. CI shows check, clippy, test-all, test-quickwit, test-none and CodeQL. If review stalls for a week or more, ping once on the PR or ask on Discord.

decision.choice: Write a PR title that reads as a changelog line, and add a CHANGELOG.md entry only if asked
decision.why: The README allows CHANGELOG edits, but the repo's update-changelog skill builds entries from merged PRs and their diffs, and CHANGELOG edits conflict easily between PRs. A clear title serves both.

alternatives.name: Add the CHANGELOG entry yourself
alternatives.tradeoff: Explicitly welcomed by the README; expect rebase conflicts on a busy unreleased section.

alternatives.name: Split into stacked PRs
alternatives.tradeoff: Right for a refactor plus fix; more coordination for a small maintainer team.

verify: The PR links the issue and shows the failing test and its fix
All CI jobs are green after your last push
Every review comment has a reply or a follow-up commit

steps.title: Write up the Tantivy contribution and pick the next rung
steps.learn: The write-up has four parts: the one question, numbers for every claim with machine and command, why surprising results happened, and what it does not prove. Next rungs: a block WAND or intersection speedup with bench evidence, an aggregation feature, or helping in tantivy-py bindings.
verify: The write-up states the one question the PR answered
Every number has the machine, toolchain and exact command
It explains at least one surprise and lists assumptions and limits

projects.problem: Tantivy is a Rust full-text search library inspired by Lucene; contributing teaches postings, BM25, segments and Rust performance work.
projects.proveIt: A PR to quickwit-oss/tantivy that passes CI and gets maintainer review, plus a write-up with test and bench numbers.
projects.hardware: Linux, macOS or Windows with stable Rust (README); Cargo.toml sets rust-version 1.88; nightly toolchain for rustfmt

projects.title: Apache Lucene
projects.question: How do you get a tested change into Apache Lucene's search core and through committer review on GitHub?

steps.title: Set the target and read Lucene's contribution and AI rules
steps.learn: Lucene is an Apache project under Apache-2.0. PRs go to main on GitHub and committers backport them. Keep discussion on the dev and user lists, not private email. AI_POLICY.md bans autonomous agents and AI-written comments. CONTRIBUTING mentions no CLA or DCO sign-off for PRs.

decision.choice: Aim at core search (org.apache.lucene.search); success is green CI and committer review
decision.why: Search scorers and queries are central, heavily tested with randomized tests, and bugs reproduce in small unit tests. The module:core/search label is added from changed paths, which helps reviewers find your PR. A merge depends on committer time, so review itself is the first milestone.

alternatives.name: Analysis modules (lucene/analysis)
alternatives.tradeoff: Bounded and test-friendly; often needs language knowledge and has less to teach about search internals.

alternatives.name: Vectors and HNSW (core/hnsw, codecs)
alternatives.tradeoff: Active, high-impact area; changes need careful benchmark evidence and longer review.

verify: Read CONTRIBUTING.md and AI_POLICY.md and list three things each requires of you
Subscribe to the dev mailing list from the discussion page
Confirm LICENSE.txt is Apache License 2.0

steps.title: Build Lucene with the Gradle wrapper on JDK 25
steps.learn: Install JDK 25 (README) and always use ./gradlew, never a system gradle. The first run writes a machine-specific gradle.properties. ./gradlew helpWorkflow and ./gradlew help list guides. On Windows clone with core.autocrlf=false since some file checksums are verified. ./gradlew check also needs Perl and Python 3.

decision.choice: Start with module-scoped tasks such as ./gradlew -p lucene/core test
decision.why: help/workflow.md and help/tests.md show module and single-class runs; they give a fast loop on the code you will touch while still using the same randomized test runner as CI.

alternatives.name: Full ./gradlew check
alternatives.tradeoff: Closest to what CI validates; long, and needs Perl and Python 3 installed.

alternatives.name: IntelliJ built-in test runner
alternatives.tradeoff: Faster for single tests per CONTRIBUTING; some tests do not run correctly in that mode.

verify: java -version reports 25 and ./gradlew runs without a system gradle
./gradlew -p lucene/core test --tests TestDemo passes
Re-running a test with -Ptests.seed=<seed> gives the same result

steps.title: Trace a query from SearchFiles through IndexSearcher to a Scorer
steps.learn: The demo SearchFiles.java parses text with the classic QueryParser and StandardAnalyzer, then calls IndexSearcher.search(query, n). IndexSearcher calls createWeight, then searchLeaf per segment, where the Weight yields a Scorer or BulkScorer feeding TopScoreDocCollector. Default similarity: BM25Similarity.
verify: Step through TestDemo in a debugger and note each frame from IndexSearcher.search to the Scorer
Find where the postings reader in codecs/lucene104 is reached for a TermQuery
Write the call chain as class:method pairs in your notes

steps.title: Learn dynamic pruning and block postings, then pick a module
steps.learn: Top-k disjunctions skip documents that cannot beat the current k-th score using per-block score bounds (impacts): see WANDScorer, MaxScoreBulkScorer and ImpactsDISI in core/search. Postings are block encoded (ForUtil, PForUtil in codecs/lucene104). Immutable segments are merged by policies like TieredMergePolicy.

decision.choice: Target core search scorers and queries (lucene/core, org.apache.lucene.search)
decision.why: Correctness bugs there are assertable in small randomized tests, lucene/benchmark-jmh has JMH benchmarks for it (MaxScoreBulkScorerFilterBenchmark, PhraseScorerBenchmark), and the concepts transfer to every engine built on Lucene.

alternatives.name: Codecs (core/codecs)
alternatives.tradeoff: Learn on-disk formats deeply; format changes need backward-codec work and strong performance evidence.

alternatives.name: Query parsers (lucene/queryparser)
alternatives.tradeoff: Self-contained grammar work; behavior changes affect user query syntax and need care.

verify: Explain why a per-block max score lets MaxScoreBulkScorer skip documents safely
Locate where BM25Similarity computes the score used by a TermQuery scorer
Name the codec package the current default postings format lives in

links.label: Lemire and Boytsov: vectorized integer decoding

steps.title: Start with a test or javadoc PR in lucene/core
steps.learn: CONTRIBUTING says a test case showing a bug is a good contribution by itself. Tests extend LuceneTestCase (lucene/test-framework) and use random() and newDirectory() so each run explores new inputs. Labels type:test and type:documentation exist, and a labeler adds module:* labels from changed paths.

decision.choice: A randomized test that pins an untested edge case in a core search class
decision.why: It teaches LuceneTestCase, seeds and beasting, which you need for any later fix, and it is easy for a committer to accept because it changes no production code.

alternatives.name: Javadoc fix
alternatives.tradeoff: Smallest possible PR; teaches less about the test framework and may wait longer for a reviewer.

alternatives.name: Build or tooling cleanup
alternatives.tradeoff: Useful if you know Gradle; touches build-infra, which many PRs depend on, so review is cautious.

steps.delegate: In apache/lucene (Java, JDK 25), add a test in lucene/core/src/test/org/apache/lucene/search/ for <Class> covering <edge case>. Extend LuceneTestCase from lucene/test-framework, use random() and newDirectory(), close readers and directories, no wildcard imports. Format with ./gradlew tidy. Run ./gradlew -p lucene/core test --tests <TestClass> -Ptests.iters=20 and report any seed that fails. Do not change production code.
verify: The test passes with -Ptests.iters=20 on several random seeds
./gradlew tidy leaves no diff afterwards
You can explain what each random choice in the test covers

steps.title: Reproduce a Lucene bug as a seeded failing test
steps.learn: Pick an open issue labeled type:bug or good first issue with no assignee and recent comments; CONTRIBUTING suggests issues nobody has started, not controversial, and self-contained. Randomized failures come with a seed: rerun with -Ptests.seed and repeat with -Ptests.iters to confirm the failure is deterministic.

decision.choice: Reproduce as a LuceneTestCase test in the module that owns the bug
decision.why: It becomes the regression test the CONTRIBUTING guide asks for (fails before the fix), runs in PR CI on Linux, ARM Linux and Windows, and lets reviewers replay your seed exactly.

alternatives.name: Standalone program on a release jar
alternatives.tradeoff: Matches what users report; not mergeable, and the bug may already be fixed on main.

alternatives.name: luceneutil run
alternatives.tradeoff: Right for performance regressions; far too heavy for a correctness bug.

verify: The test fails on main with a fixed -Ptests.seed for the reason in the issue
It fails consistently across -Ptests.iters=10 with that seed
You posted the repro and seed on the issue

steps.title: Fix the bug test first and keep the public API stable
steps.learn: Committers backport merged changes to maintenance branches when possible, so a minimal, API-compatible fix travels further. Code must pass google-java-format (./gradlew tidy), the wildcard-import check and forbiddenApis rules. Per AI_POLICY.md you must explain every line in your own words.

decision.choice: A minimal fix on main with no public API change
decision.why: Small API-stable fixes are easy to backport and review; an API change means a CHANGES.txt API Changes entry and likely dev list discussion.

alternatives.name: API change with deprecation
alternatives.tradeoff: Sometimes the right fix; needs discussion, migration notes and a longer review.

alternatives.name: Broader refactor
alternatives.tradeoff: Only after committers agree on the issue; much larger diff and backport risk.

steps.delegate: Repo apache/lucene, Java, JDK 25, Gradle wrapper. First add a failing LuceneTestCase test in <module>/src/test reproducing <issue> with seed <seed>; confirm it fails. Then make the minimal fix with no public API change. Run ./gradlew tidy, follow forbiddenApis, no wildcard imports. Run ./gradlew -p <module> test and the new test with -Ptests.iters=20. Explain each changed line; I will write the PR text myself per AI_POLICY.md.
verify: You can explain every changed line without the agent's notes
The new test fails before the fix and passes after it with the same seed
./gradlew -p <module> check passes

steps.title: Pass tidy, prek and gradle check the way CI runs them
steps.learn: CI runs uv run prek --all-files (lint), ./gradlew check -x test on JDK 25 and 27, and ./gradlew test on Linux, ARM Linux and Windows (macOS only on schedule). Locally ./gradlew check may skip slow tasks such as errorprone that CI runs. Use ./gradlew tidy for formatting and uvx prek for precommit hooks (needs uv).

decision.choice: Run ./gradlew tidy, uvx prek and ./gradlew check -x test, then module tests
decision.why: This mirrors the lint and non-test CI jobs, which catch most first-PR failures (formatting, wildcard imports, forbidden APIs), without paying for the full multi-module test run locally.

alternatives.name: Full ./gradlew check
alternatives.tradeoff: Closest to CI including all tests; much longer, best before a final push.

alternatives.name: prek as a git hook
alternatives.tradeoff: Install with prek install so checks run on every commit; slower commits, fewer red CI runs.

verify: ./gradlew tidy produces no further diff
uvx prek --all-files passes
./gradlew check -x test passes and module tests are green

steps.title: Back a performance claim with JMH or luceneutil
steps.learn: CONTRIBUTING points to luceneutil (the nightly benchmark suite) for changes that may affect performance. One-off JMH benchmarks go in the PR description; only lasting ones belong in lucene/benchmark-jmh. Build with ./gradlew :lucene:benchmark-jmh:assemble and run via java --module-path; -prof perfasm shows assembly.

decision.choice: luceneutil for query-level changes, JMH for a tight inner loop
decision.why: Query changes interact with real postings, caching and JIT warmup, which luceneutil captures; a kernel like decoding or a bitset loop is better isolated in JMH, where you can profile assembly.

alternatives.name: lucene/benchmark module
alternatives.tradeoff: Built in and off the shelf; luceneutil is what reviewers compare against nightly results.

alternatives.name: JMH only
alternatives.tradeoff: Fast and precise for a kernel; can miss end to end regressions reviewers will ask about.

verify: Report baseline vs candidate per task with variance over repeated runs
Record JDK version, CPU, OS and heap settings
One-off JMH code stays out of the diff; numbers are in the PR description

steps.title: Open the PR against main and keep it moving
steps.learn: The PR template has a Description section pointing to CONTRIBUTING. Write it in your own words. A bot labels PRs stale after 14 days without activity and suggests notifying dev@lucene.apache.org; it does not close them. CONTRIBUTING asks for patience and friendly reminders after a few days.

decision.choice: Add a CHANGES.txt entry: GITHUB#<number>, description, your name, in the right section
decision.why: CONTRIBUTING describes this format and lucene/CHANGES.txt groups entries by version and section (API Changes, New Features, Improvements, Optimizations, Bug Fixes, Build, Other and more), which saves the committer work.

alternatives.name: Leave the entry to the committer
alternatives.tradeoff: CONTRIBUTING says you may add one, not must; risk of a review round trip asking for it.

alternatives.name: No entry for a test-only PR
alternatives.tradeoff: A skip-changelog label exists; confirm with the reviewer that it applies.

verify: The PR description is written by you and links the issue
All CI jobs are green and the module label was applied
Every review comment has a reply; if stale after 2 weeks you emailed the dev list

steps.title: Write up the Lucene contribution and pick the next rung
steps.learn: The write-up has four parts: the one question, numbers for every claim with machine, JDK and command (including test seeds), why surprising results happened, and what it does not prove. Next rungs: a pruning or postings optimization with luceneutil evidence, or helping review other PRs on the dev list.
verify: The write-up states the one question the PR answered
Every number lists machine, JDK and the exact gradle or java command
It explains at least one surprise and lists assumptions and limits

projects.title: Sentence Transformers
projects.question: Can you land a reviewed fix in Sentence Transformers' embedding training code, with a regression test and before/after evidence?

steps.title: Frame a Sentence Transformers contribution and read its rules
steps.learn: You will aim at the dense embedding path (sentence_transformers/sentence_transformer/). Success is a PR that passes the Quality and Unit tests workflows and gets review. CONTRIBUTING.md sets 8 rules: own every line, give a runnable reproducer, disclose big AI help. No CLA, DCO or chat channel is named.
verify: List the 8 numbered guidelines in CONTRIBUTING.md and note the exact AI disclosure rule
Confirm LICENSE is Apache-2.0 and that CONTRIBUTING.md asks for no CLA or sign-off
Read 3 recently merged outside PRs and note how they report test commands and results

steps.title: Install Sentence Transformers editable and run pytest
steps.learn: It is a pure Python setuptools package on torch and transformers 5.x. pytest's addopts skip tests marked slow or custom, and many tests download tiny models from the Hub. CI installs with uv: '.[train,merge]' plus the test dependency group, then runs pytest over tests/.

decision.choice: A virtualenv with python -m pip install -e ".[dev]" and pre-commit install, as CONTRIBUTING.md says
decision.why: An editable install means every edit is picked up by tests immediately, and the dev extra pulls in pytest, pytest-xdist, peft, faiss-cpu and the other test dependencies in one command.

alternatives.name: uv with the test dependency group, like CI
alternatives.tradeoff: Closest to CI's resolver and extras, useful when a failure only shows in CI; needs uv and you must add -e yourself.

alternatives.name: pip install sentence-transformers from PyPI
alternatives.tradeoff: Fine for trying the API, but you cannot test changes and the release lags main.

verify: pytest tests/sentence_transformer/losses passes on a clean clone of main
Record your Python, torch and transformers versions and the time the full default pytest run takes
pre-commit run --all-files reports no changes on an untouched checkout

steps.title: Trace one encode() call from text to embedding
steps.learn: SentenceTransformer (sentence_transformer/model.py) extends BaseModel (base/model.py, an nn.Sequential). encode() calls _inference, which length-sorts and batches inputs, then preprocess and the modules: base/modules/transformer.py, sentence_transformer/modules/pooling.py. util/quantization.py packs binary output.
verify: print(SentenceTransformer('all-MiniLM-L6-v2')) and name the file defining each listed module
Break in _inference and record the feature keys returned by preprocess for one batch
encode(..., precision='binary') returns 48 bytes per 384-dim vector; find the np.packbits line that explains it

steps.title: Learn in-batch negative losses and pick your target area
steps.learn: Most retrieval models here train with MultipleNegativesRankingLoss: each anchor must score its positive above every other document in the batch (InfoNCE). Its docstring notes scale=20 equals temperature 0.05. MatryoshkaLoss wraps a loss so truncated embeddings still work. The loss overview maps data formats to losses.

decision.choice: Target sentence_transformer/losses and the matching files in tests/sentence_transformer/losses
decision.why: Each loss is a self-contained module, many have a test file in tests/sentence_transformer/losses (some do not, a gap you can fill), the math is checkable by hand on a tiny batch, and tests run on CPU.

alternatives.name: sentence_transformer/evaluation
alternatives.tradeoff: Metrics like NDCG and MRR are easy to check by hand and good for a first bug, but teach less about training dynamics.

alternatives.name: cross_encoder or sparse_encoder
alternatives.tradeoff: Pick these if you care about rerankers or SPLADE style sparse retrieval; separate model classes and test trees to learn first.

verify: Compute MultipleNegativesRankingLoss by hand for a 3 pair batch and match the library value to 1e-5
Explain why a larger batch adds negatives for this loss but not for CosineSimilarityLoss
Write down which test file covers the loss you chose and what it asserts

steps.title: Land a verified docstring or example fix first
steps.learn: Docs are Sphinx sources in docs/ (reStructuredText or MyST Markdown) plus Google-style docstrings rendered by autodoc; training scripts live in examples/. CONTRIBUTING.md asks that snippets stay runnable. Build a preview with uv pip install --group docs, then make docs, and open docs/_build/index.html.

decision.choice: Fix a wrong or stale docstring or snippet in the area you chose, proven by running it
decision.why: It exercises the whole loop (fork, pre-commit, CI, review) on a low-risk diff, and running the snippet proves the fix instead of asserting it, which CONTRIBUTING.md asks for.

alternatives.name: Add a missing regression test
alternatives.tradeoff: More valuable to maintainers, but you need to show what behavior is untested and why it matters.

alternatives.name: Spelling or style sweeps
alternatives.tradeoff: The typos hook already catches many, and CONTRIBUTING.md warns against repeated submissions of the same pattern.

verify: make docs builds and the changed page renders correctly in docs/_build
The snippet you touched runs end to end against your editable install
The diff touches one topic and pre-commit passes

steps.title: Pick a bug issue and turn it into a failing test
steps.learn: The good first issue and good second issue labels exist but had no open issues when checked; open issues labeled bug are the realistic pool. The repo gets many outside PRs, so search open and closed PRs before starting. A reproducer should name versions and say if you hit the bug in real use.

decision.choice: An open bug issue with a reproducer, no linked PR, and a maintainer reply that confirms it
decision.why: Confirmation means the fix is wanted, and an existing reproducer gives you the failing test almost for free. Checking for linked PRs avoids the competing fixes CONTRIBUTING.md asks you not to open.

alternatives.name: A bug you hit in your own use
alternatives.tradeoff: Strongest evidence of impact, but open an issue with a reproducer first so maintainers can agree it is a bug.

alternatives.name: A bug found by reading code
alternatives.tradeoff: Allowed, but you must say so, and without a realistic affected workflow it may be judged not worth the review time.

verify: The reproducer runs in under a minute on CPU with a tiny model and shows the wrong result
A new test in the matching tests/ file fails on main for exactly the reported reason
You searched open and closed PRs and issues for duplicates and linked any you found

steps.title: Fix the root cause with a test-first agent prompt
steps.learn: CONTRIBUTING.md asks you to fix the cause, follow existing patterns, and keep existing models and public functions producing the same outputs. If the cause is in transformers or huggingface_hub, report it upstream and justify any local workaround. You own every line the agent writes.

decision.choice: Fix it inside Sentence Transformers when the root cause is in this repo
decision.why: The fix and its regression test live next to each other, review stays in one repo, and you can show unchanged outputs for existing models.

alternatives.name: Fix upstream in transformers
alternatives.tradeoff: Correct when the cause is there; slower, a different review culture, and you link it from this repo's issue.

alternatives.name: Local workaround plus upstream report
alternatives.tradeoff: Unblocks users sooner, but must explain why the workaround is needed and costs future cleanup.

steps.delegate: In huggingface/sentence-transformers (Python 3.10+, ruff with line length 119, Google-style docstrings, every module starts with from __future__ import annotations), first add a failing pytest test in tests/sentence_transformer/<area>/ that reproduces: <issue summary>, reusing its tiny models. Then make the smallest root-cause fix in sentence_transformers/; keep public signatures and existing model outputs unchanged. Run that test file and pre-commit run --all-files. Explain each change.
verify: The new test fails on main and passes with the fix
Embeddings from a pretrained model are torch.allclose before and after the change
You can explain every changed line without the agent, and you noted the AI help for the PR

steps.title: Run pre-commit and the CI test subset locally
steps.learn: Quality runs make check (pre-commit run -a: ruff-check --fix, ruff-format, typos). Unit tests runs python -m pytest --durations 20 -sv tests/ on Python 3.10 to 3.14, Ubuntu and Windows. Minimum version tests reruns on the lowest supported dependencies. Slow and custom tests are skipped.

decision.choice: pre-commit on every commit, the touched test folders while iterating, and one full pytest before review
decision.why: Mirrors both CI workflows at a fraction of the cost, and the final full run catches breakage in other model types that share base/ code.

alternatives.name: pytest -n auto with pytest-xdist
alternatives.tradeoff: pytest-xdist is in the dev extra and speeds up a full run on many cores; parallel output is harder to read when something fails.

alternatives.name: Rely on CI only
alternatives.tradeoff: Saves local time, but red CI on a PR costs maintainer attention, which CONTRIBUTING.md says is limited.

verify: make check passes with no files modified
Touched test folders pass on Python 3.10, the oldest version CI tests
One full default pytest run is green, and you note any checks you could not run

steps.title: Measure encode throughput before and after a change
steps.learn: CONTRIBUTING.md requires before and after measurements for any performance claim. examples/sentence_transformer/evaluation/evaluation_inference_speed.py encodes up to 100k all-nli sentences three times with torch limited to 4 threads. The efficiency docs compare ONNX and OpenVINO backends.

decision.choice: Use the inference speed example, pinned to one model and thread count, on main and on your branch
decision.why: It is the repo's own harness, it measures encode end to end the way users call it, and fixed threads reduce noise on a laptop.

alternatives.name: Microbenchmark one function
alternatives.tradeoff: Isolates your change with less noise, but may not show up in end to end encode time.

alternatives.name: Backend comparison as in the efficiency docs
alternatives.tradeoff: Right for ONNX or OpenVINO changes; needs the onnx or openvino extras and more setup.

verify: At least 3 runs per side with mean and spread reported
CPU model, thread count, torch version and batch size are recorded
Outputs are allclose between main and your branch for a performance-only change

steps.title: Open a focused PR with evidence and handle review
steps.learn: There is no PR template; CONTRIBUTING.md accepts any format that has the description, validation (commands run, results, checks not run) and AI disclosure. Link the issue. Maintainers may close unverified, duplicate or costly PRs, so keep the diff small and answer review in your own words.

decision.choice: One PR with the test and fix, linked to the issue, rebased on main
decision.why: A single small diff with its own evidence is the cheapest thing for a busy maintainer to review and matches guideline 6 on focused submissions.

alternatives.name: Draft PR early
alternatives.tradeoff: Good when the design is unclear and you want direction; mark it clearly so it is not reviewed as finished.

alternatives.name: Several PRs per instance of a pattern
alternatives.tradeoff: CONTRIBUTING.md asks to group related mechanical fixes instead; only split truly independent changes.

verify: The PR description lists the exact test commands and their results
AI assistance is disclosed if it wrote a substantial part
Quality and Unit tests checks are green, and every review comment has a reply or a commit

steps.title: Write up the Sentence Transformers fix and pick the next rung
steps.learn: Record the bug, the root cause, how you proved it (failing test, unchanged outputs, timings), and what review taught you. Next rungs: a new evaluator option, a loss improvement with a training comparison, or work in cross_encoder or sparse_encoder.
verify: The write-up states the bug, the root cause and the PR link
Every claim has a number or a test name, with machine and versions
It names one concrete next contribution and why

projects.problem: Hugging Face's Python library for embedding, reranker, sparse and multi-vector models; contributing teaches contrastive losses, evaluators and tested ML APIs.
projects.proveIt: A PR with a regression test that passes the Quality, Unit tests and Minimum version tests workflows and gets maintainer review, plus a write-up
projects.hardware: Any laptop with Python 3.10+; CI tests run on CPU-only runners and download small models from the Hugging Face Hub
projects.aiPolicy: AI assistance is welcome, but you must read and be able to explain every changed line, and briefly disclose significant AI-generated code or text in the PR description.

projects.title: pgvector
projects.question: Can you reproduce and fix a real pgvector bug in C, prove it with Postgres regression tests, and get it reviewed by its maintainer?

steps.title: Frame a pgvector contribution and its single-maintainer reality
steps.learn: The guide is the README Contributing section; there is no CONTRIBUTING file, code of conduct, CLA, DCO or AI policy. When checked, 98 of the last 100 commits were by maintainer ankane and 20 of the last 100 closed PRs were merged. Review is the realistic goal; a merge is a bonus.
verify: Read the README Contributing section and list its test and debug build commands
Read LICENSE and confirm it is the PostgreSQL License (the GitHub API reports NOASSERTION)
Read 5 recently closed outside PRs and note how each was resolved

steps.title: Build pgvector with assertions and run both test suites
steps.learn: The Makefile uses PGXS from pg_config and adds auto-vectorization flags (and -march=native on most platforms). make and make install build it; make installcheck runs pg_regress over test/sql; make prove_installcheck runs Perl TAP tests in test/t and needs IPC::Run. Single tests: REGRESS=name or PROVE_TESTS=path.

decision.choice: Packaged Postgres with server dev files, built with PG_CFLAGS="-DUSE_ASSERT_CHECKING"
decision.why: It is the README's own setup, it is quick to rebuild, and assertions inside pgvector catch many bugs your change could introduce.

alternatives.name: Postgres built from source with cassert and TAP
alternatives.tradeoff: Also asserts inside Postgres itself and gives TAP support anywhere; costs a longer one-time build.

alternatives.name: Homebrew Postgres on macOS
alternatives.tradeoff: Easy to install, but CI notes it lacks TAP support, so you must download Postgres sources for the Perl test modules.

alternatives.name: The repo Dockerfile
alternatives.tradeoff: Good for trying a release, but it fetches a tagged release from GitHub, not your local edits.

verify: CREATE EXTENSION vector succeeds and extversion matches EXTVERSION in the Makefile
make installcheck passes every regression test
make prove_installcheck PROVE_TESTS=test/t/012_hnsw_vector_build_recall.pl passes

steps.title: Trace an L2 nearest-neighbor query through the HNSW scan
steps.learn: sql/vector.sql creates the types, the L2 distance operator, opclasses like vector_l2_ops and the hnsw access method. hnswhandler in src/hnsw.c fills the IndexAmRoutine; the planner calls hnswcostestimate; hnswgettuple in src/hnswscan.c calls HnswSearchLayer in src/hnswutils.c; distances come from src/vector.c.
verify: EXPLAIN shows an Index Scan on your hnsw index for an ORDER BY L2 distance LIMIT 5 query
Find where hnsw.ef_search is defined in src/hnsw.c and where src/hnswscan.c uses it
In a debugger, hit hnswgettuple and list each call down to vector_l2_squared_distance (the opclass support function)

steps.title: Learn HNSW inside Postgres and choose a subsystem
steps.learn: HNSW is a layered graph searched greedily. In pgvector the defaults are m 16, ef_construction 64 and hnsw.ef_search 40; the graph lives in Postgres pages written with generic WAL records. WHERE filters apply after the index scan, so iterative scans (since 0.8.0) keep scanning until enough rows match.

decision.choice: Target the HNSW code: src/hnsw*.c and its TAP tests
decision.why: It is the most used index, its behaviors (recall, inserts, vacuum, iterative scans) each have numbered TAP tests to extend, and it teaches graph ANN plus Postgres storage together.

alternatives.name: IVFFlat (src/ivf*.c)
alternatives.tradeoff: Smaller code with a k-means build; simpler to follow, but less used now that HNSW exists.

alternatives.name: Types and distances (vector.c, halfvec.c, sparsevec.c)
alternatives.tradeoff: Input parsing and SIMD-friendly distance loops, testable with pg_regress alone; less about indexing.

verify: Explain in two sentences why an HNSW index returns fewer rows with a selective WHERE clause
Measure recall@10 at hnsw.ef_search 10, 40 and 100 against an exact scan on 100k random vectors
Find the GenericXLog calls in src/hnswutils.c and say what they protect

steps.title: Start with a regression test for an untested edge case
steps.learn: Regression tests are SQL files in test/sql with expected output in test/expected, compared by pg_regress; the Makefile builds the REGRESS list from test/sql automatically. TAP tests in test/t cover WAL, vacuum, recall and concurrency. The README is the only user documentation.

decision.choice: Add pg_regress cases for an untested edge in input parsing, casts or dimension limits
decision.why: Pure SQL tests are small, deterministic and run in seconds on every CI platform, so they are cheap for a single maintainer to review.

alternatives.name: A README clarification
alternatives.tradeoff: Useful when docs and behavior disagree; the README is long and maintainer curated, so keep it to one fact.

alternatives.name: A new TAP test
alternatives.tradeoff: Needed for recall, WAL or concurrency behavior; requires Perl and IPC::Run and is slower to run.

verify: The new cases appear in both test/sql and test/expected
make installcheck REGRESS=<file> passes with an assert-enabled build
You confirmed no existing test already covers the case

steps.title: Reproduce an open pgvector issue as a failing test
steps.learn: Default labels like bug and good first issue exist but were applied to no issues when checked, and only about a dozen issues were open, many of them questions. Read each open issue, rebuild the setup in a fresh database, and record Postgres version, pgvector version, OS and index settings.

decision.choice: Reproduce one open issue as a SQL script, then as a pg_regress or TAP test
decision.why: A failing test is the clearest evidence for a maintainer who writes most of the code, and it guards the fix across the CI matrix.

alternatives.name: Stress an assert build
