projects.title: Hugging Face Transformers
projects.question: Can I diagnose and fix a real bug in Hugging Face Transformers by hand, with a reproducer, and get it through CI and maintainer review?

steps.title: Read the Transformers code agent policy and PR rules
steps.learn: Goal: one coordinated PR that passes CI and gets review. The repo is flooded with agent PRs, so first-time contributors must write their PR and issue themselves and tick a box saying so; busywork PRs (single typos, style tweaks) are discouraged. Apache-2.0, no CLA or DCO. Questions go to the forum or Discord.

steps.title: Install Transformers editable and run Llama's tests on CPU
steps.learn: There is no compile step: Transformers is pure Python on top of PyTorch. CONTRIBUTING lists three extras: [dev] for most work, [torch,testing] for model work, [quality] for docs. Fast tests use tiny random configs and run on CPU; @slow tests download real checkpoints and need RUN_SLOW=1.

decision.choice: pip install -e ".[dev]" in a fresh venv with a CPU or CUDA PyTorch build
decision.why: [dev] includes the style and quality tools that make style and make check-repo need, so you can run every local check the CI runs without a second install.

alternatives.name: pip install -e ".[torch,testing]"
alternatives.tradeoff: Lighter than [dev] (skips vision, audio and other optional extras) and still includes the quality tools; some model tests may skip for missing optional deps.

alternatives.name: pip install -e ".[quality]"
alternatives.tradeoff: Smallest, for docs-only changes; cannot run model tests.

steps.learn: AutoModelForCausalLM (models/auto/modeling_auto.py) maps a config to LlamaForCausalLM; from_pretrained in modeling_utils.py loads weights. generate (generation/utils.py) calls _sample, which runs forward in models/llama/modeling_llama.py; attention uses ALL_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS and a DynamicCache.

steps.learn: Model files do not inherit from each other. New models are written as modular_<name>.py files (modular_gemma.py imports from llama) and make fix-repo generates modeling_*.py; never edit a generated file. Legacy # Copied from blocks are re-synced, so edit their source.

alternatives.name: generation/ or cache_utils.py
alternatives.tradeoff: High impact, but changing core files triggers all model tests and reviewers are cautious.

alternatives.name: Tokenizers or pipelines
alternatives.tradeoff: Smaller blast radius and CPU-friendly; bugs often depend on specific checkpoints you must download.

steps.learn: Single-typo and style-only PRs are discouraged as busywork; meaningful doc fixes (missing content, wrong examples) are welcome as direct PRs. CONTRIBUTING values clear diagnosis and a simple reproducer you actually ran, and warns against theoretical bugs that rarely matter in practice. ISSUES.md explains what a good report includes.

alternatives.tradeoff: CONTRIBUTING asks to bundle mechanical cleanups into one systematic scope, but a larger diff is slower to review; avoid it for a first PR.

projects.title: OR-Tools
projects.question: How do you get a tested fix into Google's OR-Tools CP-SAT solver and through review on a repo that mostly syncs from Google's internal code?

steps.title: Set the target: a reviewed CP-SAT PR to OR-Tools main
steps.learn: OR-Tools is Google's C++ optimization suite (CP-SAT, routing, GLOP, PDLP, MathOpt) with Python, Java, C# and Go wrappers. Most history lands as maintainer exports from Google's internal repo; outside PRs merge, but only a few a month. Aim for a small CP-SAT PR that passes presubmit and gets review.
verify: You signed the Google CLA at cla.developers.google.com with the email you commit with
You read CONTRIBUTING.md and the PR template, which says to target main, not the default stable branch
You know modeling questions go to the or-tools-discuss group or Discord, and GitHub issues are for bugs

steps.title: Build OR-Tools with Bazel and run the CP-SAT tests
steps.learn: Three builds exist: Bazel (bazel/README.md), CMake (cmake/README.md, with BUILD_PYTHON for the wheel) and legacy Make. The .bazelrc sets C++20. Presubmit runs bazel build and test with --config=ci over //ortools/... plus a CMake matrix for cpp, java, dotnet and python.

decision.choice: Clone main and use Bazel: bazel test -c opt //ortools/sat/python:cp_model_test //ortools/sat:cp_model_presolve_test
decision.why: Bazel builds only the targets you ask for, which keeps the loop short on a big C++ tree, and the sat BUILD.bazel defines both C++ (or_cc_test) and Python (py_test) tests. Both targets here are tagged noci, so presubmit (--config=ci) skips them; running them locally is the only check they get.

alternatives.name: CMake with -DBUILD_PYTHON=ON and ctest
alternatives.tradeoff: Pick it to work on the Python wheel or packaging, as cmake/docs/python.md shows (target python_package, ctest -R "python_.*"). It builds far more, with BUILD_DEPS fetching dependencies.

alternatives.name: pip install ortools only
alternatives.tradeoff: Fine for writing a reproducer against a release, but it gives you a stable build with no tests and no way to change C++ code.

verify: bazel test -c opt //ortools/sat/python:cp_model_test passes on your machine
You recorded OS, compiler, Bazel version and wall time for the first build
git branch shows you on main, not stable

steps.title: Trace one Python solve() call down to CP-SAT search
steps.learn: In ortools/sat/python/cp_model.py, CpModel builds a CpModelProto (cp_model.proto) and CpSolver.solve hands it to SolveWrapper (pybind11 in pybind_solver.cc, swig_helper.h). That calls SolveCpModel in cp_model_solver.cc: validation, PresolveCpModel, then LoadCpModel and SolveLoadedCpModel per subsolver.
verify: You can name the file and function for each hop from CpSolver.solve to SolveCpModel
You ran a sample with log_search_progress on and matched log sections to presolve and subsolvers
You found where ValidateCpModel (cp_model_checker.h) rejects a bad model

steps.title: Learn how CP-SAT mixes SAT, CP and LP, then pick an area
steps.learn: CP-SAT is a CP solver with clause learning built on a SAT core: integer variables get lazily encoded, propagators explain their deductions as clauses, LP relaxations add cuts, and many subsolvers (LNS, feasibility jump) share bounds and solutions in parallel. The sat README links a CPAIOR 2020 masterclass.

decision.choice: Target CP-SAT's model layer: validation, presolve rules or the Python API in ortools/sat
decision.why: Recent merged outside PRs touch exactly this (int_div validation, LNS determinism). Bugs there reproduce with a tiny model, each file has a matching _test.cc or _test.py, and you avoid deep propagator invariants on your first change.

alternatives.name: Routing solver (ortools/routing)
alternatives.tradeoff: Many labeled issues (Routing - cost, breaks, side constraints), but the local search code is large and bugs often need bigger instances to reproduce.

alternatives.name: MathOpt or linear_solver wrappers
alternatives.tradeoff: Good if you know a solver backend like HiGHS or Xpress; fixes often need that third party solver installed or licensed to test.

verify: You can explain in two sentences why presolve needs a postsolve mapping
You solved a ortools/sat/samples model and read its presolve summary in the log
You wrote down the target files and their test files

steps.title: Land a first CP-SAT sample, docstring or test fix
steps.learn: Samples in ortools/sat/samples are real Bazel tests (py_test, or_cc_test), and ortools/sat/docs embeds snippets from them. A typo fix in a comment was merged recently, so small PRs do get through. Expect slow review; the core team is small.

decision.choice: Fix a docstring or add a missing test case in ortools/sat/python, one concern per PR
decision.why: cp_model.py is user facing and covered by cp_model_test.py, so a fix is easy to verify and easy for a maintainer to review. It also gets your CLA and branch setup working before a real bug fix.

alternatives.name: New sample in ortools/sat/samples
alternatives.tradeoff: Useful, but samples come in several languages and docs pull from them, so maintainers may want matching versions; more review.

alternatives.name: Docs fix under ortools/sat/docs
alternatives.tradeoff: Lowest risk, but issues labeled Doc: Optimization Site concern the external website, which is not in this repo.

verify: Your change touches one concern and the relevant Bazel test still passes
The PR targets main and the CLA check is green
You searched open PRs to make sure nobody else already fixed it

steps.title: Reproduce a CP-SAT bug as a minimal model and failing test
steps.learn: There is no good first issue label; the closest are Help Needed, Bug and Solver: CP-SAT Solver. The bug template asks for version, language, solver, OS and the model proto, so shrink a failing model to a few variables, export it, and check it on main, not only on a release.

decision.choice: Pick an open Bug plus Solver: CP-SAT Solver issue, unassigned, with recent activity and a model attached
decision.why: An attached model lets you reproduce exactly. Unassigned and recently active means nobody is mid-fix and a maintainer is still watching. Comment on the issue before coding to ask whether a PR is welcome.

alternatives.name: Issues labeled Help Needed
alternatives.tradeoff: Maintainers flagged them as wanting outside help, but there are few and several are build or platform problems needing that OS.

alternatives.name: A bug you hit yourself
alternatives.tradeoff: Strong motivation and you own the repro, but file an issue first so maintainers can say whether it is a bug or a modeling question.

verify: Your reproducer fails on a fresh main build and you noted the exact status or crash
The model is the smallest you could make it, and you can say which constraint triggers it
You posted the reproducer on the issue and got no objection to a PR

steps.title: Fix the bug test first, in Google C++ style
steps.learn: C++ follows Google style via .clang-format; C++ tests use gtest through or_cc_test, Python tests use absl.testing absltest. The repo has no written AI policy, but you sign the CLA for the code, so you must understand and defend every line.
steps.delegate: In google/or-tools on main, fix this CP-SAT bug: <issue summary + minimal model>. First add a failing test in the matching file (ortools/sat/<file>_test.cc with gtest, or ortools/sat/python/cp_model_test.py with absltest) and confirm it fails via bazel test -c opt. Then make the smallest fix in ortools/sat. Follow Google C++ style and .clang-format. Do not reformat unrelated code. Explain why the fix is sound for presolve and postsolve.
verify: The new test fails before your fix and passes after, run with bazel test -c opt
You can explain each changed line and why it does not break postsolve or other constraint types
The diff touches only the files the fix needs

steps.title: Match presubmit: clang-format and the Bazel test subset
steps.learn: Presubmit runs on PRs to main: a clang-format job (excluding .tab.hh), Bazel build and test with --config=ci (skips noci tests) on Linux and macOS, and CMake builds for cpp, java, dotnet and python. Check Format runs clang-format after pushes to main, not on PRs. No pre-commit config; Python has a .pylintrc.

decision.choice: Run clang-format --style=file --dry-run --Werror on changed files, bazel test --config=ci, then your noci test
decision.why: These mirror the presubmit clang-format and Bazel jobs, which catch most failures, while testing //ortools/sat/... instead of //ortools/... keeps the loop under your control.

alternatives.name: Full bazel test --config=ci //ortools/...
alternatives.tradeoff: Closest to CI and catches cross package breakage, but it builds and tests the whole tree, which is slow on a laptop.

alternatives.name: Rely on CI only
alternatives.tradeoff: Saves local time, but every red run costs a review round trip on a slow moving repo.

verify: clang-format dry run on your changed files prints no errors
bazel test --config=ci //ortools/sat/... passes, and the noci test you edited (e.g. //ortools/sat/python:cp_model_test) passes when run without --config=ci
pylint with the repo .pylintrc shows no new warnings for Python changes

steps.title: Measure a CP-SAT hot path with its Google Benchmark targets
steps.learn: ortools/sat has *_benchmark.cc files built as testonly or_cc_binary targets on @google_benchmark (e.g. integer_benchmark, util_benchmark, 2d_orthogonal_packing_benchmark). Solver speed claims also need a model set and fixed seeds, since parallel search is not reproducible run to run.

decision.choice: Change a helper covered by an existing benchmark and compare before and after with bazel run -c opt
decision.why: A microbenchmark isolates the code you changed, Google Benchmark reports repetitions you can turn into variance, and a reviewer can rerun the same target.

alternatives.name: End to end solve time on a model set
alternatives.tradeoff: Closer to what users feel, but noisy: you need fixed parameters (num_workers, random_seed), many runs and many models before claiming a win.

alternatives.name: Feature rung instead
alternatives.tradeoff: Pick it if your area has no benchmark; add a small parameter or API option with tests, but propose it in an issue first.

verify: You ran the benchmark with repetitions before and after on the same idle machine and report mean and spread
You recorded CPU model, OS, compiler and the exact bazel command
Tests for the touched code still pass after the change

steps.title: Open the PR against main and steer it through review
steps.learn: The template asks you to target main, not stable, and confirms the CLA. Merged outside PRs use short titles with an area prefix like sat:. Maintainers may land your change through their internal export, so the final commit can differ from yours; that still counts.
verify: The PR targets main, links the issue, and states the reproducer and the test you added
The CLA check and presubmit jobs are green, or you explained any unrelated failure
You answered each review comment and rebased on main when asked

steps.title: Write up the OR-Tools contribution and pick the next rung
steps.learn: Record what you learned about CP-SAT internals, the review experience on a Google exported repo, and any numbers with machine and command. If the PR stalled, note how long and what you did. Next rungs: a presolve rule with tests, a routing fix, or a MathOpt backend fix.
verify: The write-up states the issue, the fix, the test and the PR outcome
Every number has the machine, command and run count
It names one concrete next contribution and the files it would touch

projects.problem: OR-Tools is Google's C++ optimization suite (CP-SAT, routing, LP); contributing teaches solver internals, Bazel and Google style review
projects.proveIt: A small CP-SAT PR to main with a failing-then-passing test, green presubmit and maintainer review, plus a write-up
projects.language: C++, Python, Java, C#, Go, Julia
projects.hardware: Any recent Linux, macOS or Windows machine, CPU only; full builds are heavy, so many cores help
